column1: # Game profile of Bridge Constructor Portal (Switch, update 1.1 = v131072, with its licence-only DLC Portal Proficiency). Plays on the Mac and an iPhone, by touch alone
# Unity 2019.1.14f1 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 8.3.2, NVN API 53.313; subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie.
# The shaders are Unity shader objects in the player's serialized files and bundles under Data/, read by the shader split: 5,137 of them (2,704 vertex, 2,412 pixel, 20 compute, 1 geometry).
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile; op_mode and pad_layout added (README.md).
# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID
# handheld: the game plays by touch there, with its own touch tutorial (draw parts from an anchor with a finger, tap a part to turn it into road, double tap to remove it;
# Test, Build and Drive are buttons on screen); on the iPhone those are the touches no gamepad control takes, on the Mac the mouse. Docked it reads only the pads
# touch: the virtual gamepad starts in its Tap layout, every touch to the game; the in-game menu's Controller layout brings back 2D / 3D
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so the game takes its memory as address regions; it sets no heap. nninitStartup gives StandardAllocator the pool less what is used,
# 3.14 GB at alias +0.06 GB; Unity's own regions after it stay within the iPhone's 4.375 GB alias region (README.md, Memory).
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and its bundles
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 (the NSP script's heap check boot): the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# The game runs at 30 fps, as on the Switch (it asks for present interval 2), so no frame-rate key is needed.
